title: The Emperor's Silver Beard (HI)
summary: Akbar finds his first grey hair and feels distressed. Birbal turns the moment into a poetic celebration of mature wisdom and leadership.
full_text:
One morning, while the royal barber was trimming his beard, Emperor Akbar noticed a single, bright silver hair glinting among the black hairs of his chin. The monarch plucked the white hair, held it between his fingers, and looked down in deep melancholy.

Arriving at the Diwan-i-Khas, Akbar was somber: 'Birbal, look at this white hair. Old age has knocked upon my door. My youth has flown, and the winter of life has begun. It pains my heart to see strength fading.'

Birbal smiled with overflowing affection, stepped to the throne, and bowed low:

'Rejoice, Your Imperial Majesty! That single silver hair is the most glorious decoration that has ever adorned your brow!'

Akbar looked surprised: 'How can a sign of decaying age be glorious?'

Birbal explained with melodic eloquence:

'Sire, consider what that silver hair represents.

'It is not a mark of decay; it is an imperial crown of silver wisdom bestowed upon you by heaven!

'A young, black-bearded king may possess wild passion, fierce temper, and reckless ambition that plunges nations into war for glory.

'But that single silver hair tells your fifty million subjects that their Emperor has passed through the fires of youth, and has arrived at the golden summit of mature discernment, patience, mercy, and justice!

'White is the color of truth, of peace, and of the pure snows that feed the great rivers of Hindustan.

'Your subjects do not desire an inexperienced youth on the throne; they pray for an experienced sovereign whose silver beard reflects the light of seasoned wisdom. Celebrate the autumn of life, Sire, for autumn brings the sweetest harvest!'

Akbar's heart filled with joy and renewed dignity. He looked at his reflection in the mirror with pride, embraced Birbal, and thanked him for turning a moment of dread into an anthem of royal honor.
